Package com.egradx.observability

Class EgradxTraceContext

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.observability.EgradxTraceContext
public final class EgradxTraceContext extends Object
Where a piece of work came from, in a form that can be written into a database row or a message and picked up again later, on another thread or in another process.

It holds what a tracer's propagator writes — the W3C "traceparent" header, and "tracestate" or baggage if there is any — plus the "requestId" of the HTTP request that started it. Without a tracer only the request id is there, and that is still enough to find every log line and every row a request produced.

Immutable. Never throws on bad input: a context that cannot be read is empty, because losing a trace must never lose the work it was attached to.

      What can be known on this thread without a tracer: the request id. To capture the trace as well, start a sender observation — EgradxObservations.send(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.util.function.BiFunction<io.micrometer.observation.Observation, com.egradx.observability.EgradxTraceContext, T>).

    • serialize

      public String serialize()
      key=value&key=value, URL-encoded, at most 1024 characters. If it would be longer, everything but traceparent and the request id is left out — tracestate and baggage are hints; the trace itself is what matters. Empty for an empty context.

    • parse

      public static EgradxTraceContext parse(String serialized)
      Reads what serialize() wrote. Null, blank or unreadable text is an empty context.
